items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: I suspect, of course, it was through Paul Merez and Rapolo, and those fellows.

ctx.x: And he made arrangements. When he was working with the Gold Cat Orchestra at WGN, he would arrange mix tunes for them. He took delight in that. He arranged the Wolverine's Limehouse, which they recorded. However, that was a different Wolverine's. It was Voino's band, but a band that apparently didn't contain any of the early men. And so he was quite understanding, at any rate, and rather sophisticated for a Dixie former. Here again we come to that question, whether without New Orleans there might have been a high…

No, they did not. And I've often wondered where the influence crept in without their knowing it, and I suspect, of course, it was through Paul Merez and Rapolo, and those fellows. And Brunus. One thing that used to surprise me, I originally played with a little band around a country day school. This must have been as early as 20. Five, four pieces. Not a Dixie-Line combination at all, but with a C-molly saxophone, that kind of lead. When I graduated, I think by learning how to play an E-flat, to the New Trier…
Do you remember anybody in the San Band of that period?
